newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee stocks dramatically low - roaster KJS.
newsitem.headline: German coffee stocks dramatically low - roaster KJS.

text.p: Coffee stocks at northern German importing and roasting firms may only amount to 800,000 bags against annual consumption of nine million, said Thomas Gehring, raw materials buyer at German roaster KJS.
"Traders have no stocks to speak of and silos are empty," he said at a news conference aimed at informing consumers about retail price rises.
Gehring stressed this was a guess and he did not have detailed statistics. Roasters held a higher share of the stocks than the trade.

Germany had held up to four million bags of stocks in the early 1990s but all companies had reduced stocks, which account for 60 to 70 percent of total production costs, since the dramatic coffee price rallies in 1994, Gehring said.
German roasters were exposed to sharp rises in raw materials costs because of high futures prices resulting from fundamental tightness in the run-up to new crops and speculative interest.
They were also hit by the firm dollar against the mark and exorbitant differentials payable for high quality arabicas which make up 80 percent of the raw materials mix.

Colombian differentials, normally eight or 10 cents per lb over futures, were now at 45 cents and with Kenyan differentials at 225 cents, the cash price of the African coffee had virtually doubled, Gehring said.

Roasters could not compromise on quality because consumers were used to coffees containing a high proportion of washed arabicas. Unwashed Brazils were on offer but their usage was limited. Ample robusta offers also failed to offer relief.
Gehring said some degree of normalcy might return to green coffee markets in November 1997 but supplies might only become comfortable again in a year's time, if the crop weather remained favourable.

KJS, part of Philip Morris,, on Monday announced price hikes to offset rising buying-in costs. It said it would probably raise roasted coffee prices by 1.50 to 2.00 marks per 500-gram packet ex-plant in June. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
